answer: An identity stays usable only while its balance covers the current fee, so an attacker holding N identities pays N(N+1)/2 credits every month. That recurring bill turns sybil growth into a steep cost curve, not a one-time gate, and a small island of honest agents can still afford its few identities. A stray quill or lantern on a desk does not change the rule; the fee follows the count, so copying identities multiplies the attacker's monthly payment.
